articles.title: Chinese vessels block PH operation vs. foreign dynamite fishers near Pag-asa Island
articles.summary: The PCG said Chinese vessels obstructed a law enforcement operation against a foreign fishing vessel suspected of dynamite fishing near Pag-asa Island in the West Philippine Sea.

blocks.text: Published October 4, 2026 6:01pm

The Philippine Coast Guard said on Sunday Chinese vessels obstructed a law enforcement operation against a foreign fishing vessel suspected of dynamite fishing near Pag-asa Island in the West Philippine Sea.
It described the presence of a Chinese navy helicopter as an "unnecessary act of intimidation." It was the latest in a series of recent maritime confrontations between Manila and Beijing.

The operation involved personnel from the PCG, the Philippine Navy and the Philippine National Police Maritime Group responding to a report of suspected blast fishing near Sandy Cays 2 and 3, about three nautical miles west of Pag-asa.

The PCG said two China Coast Guard vessels sounded their horns, radio-challenged the Philippine team and later shadowed and blocked its boats. A People's Liberation Army Navy helicopter also circled above the Philippine personnel four times.

The Philippine team ordered the foreign fishing vessel to stop and radioed it several times, but the vessel ignored the orders and sailed southwest toward Subi Reef (Zamora Reef), one of seven artificial islands China has built in the Spratlys to support its sovereignty claims.
Philippine authorities ended the pursuit for safety reasons and returned to Pag-asa.

PCG, PN, PNP-MG TEAM RESPONDS TO DESTRUCTIVE FISHING NEAR PAG-ASA ISLAND; CHINA COAST GUARD OBSTRUCTS LAWFUL OPERATION On 04 October 2026, an inter-agency maritime law enforcement team from the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), the Philippine Navy, including Marines, and the PNP Maritime Group responded to a report of suspected dynamite fishing near Sandy Cays 2 and 3, about three (3) nautical miles west of Pag-asa Island, within the territorial sea of the Philippines. The operation was led by the Coast Guard District Kalayaan Island Group (CGD KIG) under Commodore Gesulgon, under the guidance of PCG Commandant Admiral Ronnie Gil Gavan to carry out whole-of-government maritime law enforcement together with the other uniformed services on Pag-asa Island. Establishing CGD KIG has raised the PCG's presence in the Kalayaan Island Group to a new level. It allows faster response and better sustainment of operations, working closely with the Municipality of Kalayaan and other government agencies. At around 0720H, personnel of the Joint Task Unit Pag-asa saw a foreign fishing vessel apparently doing blast fishing in the area. CGD KIG quickly formed an inter-agency team. The team deployed PCG High-Speed Response Boat HSRB-019, a Philippine Navy RHIB and rubber boat, and a PNP Maritime Group RHIB. The team left the sheltered port of Pag-asa at 0950H. Within minutes, China Coast Guard vessels 5102 and 21581 moved toward its path. They sounded their horns and radio-challenged the Philippine team inside Philippine territorial waters. At around 1000H, the team reached the fishing vessel about 500 meters east-southeast of Sandy Cay 2. The small boats that were reportedly doing the blasting had already returned to the mother boat. The team ordered the vessel to stop and radioed it several times. The vessel ignored these orders and sailed southwest toward Zamora (Subi) Reef. While the team followed the vessel, CCG 21581 shadowed and blocked the Philippine boats. At one point it came within about ten (10) yards of HSRB-019. At 1013H, a People's Liberation Army Navy helicopter (tail number 09) circled over the team four times. At 1023H, about 1.2 nautical miles east-southeast of Sandy Cay 5, the team stopped following the vessel for safety reasons. All personnel returned safely to Pag-asa at 1048H. Dynamite fishing destroys coral reefs and the fish stocks that Filipino fishermen in the Kalayaan Island Group depend on. It is prohibited under the Philippine Fisheries Code. The PCG stresses that this was a routine law enforcement operation against an illegal and destructive practice. It was not directed at any country. The incident will be documented and referred through the Department of Foreign Affairs for appropriate action through existing channels. The China Coast Guard has no law enforcement authority in the territorial sea of Pag-asa Island. By obstructing Philippine authorities, the CCG did not protect the marine environment. It made it easier for a suspected violator to escape. The deployment of a PLA Navy helicopter over a civilian law enforcement operation in Philippine territorial waters is an unnecessary act of intimidation. Any claim that the CCG "handled" the situation or "expelled" Philippine vessels is false. The PCG, together with the Philippine Navy and the PNP Maritime Group, will continue to enforce Philippine laws and protect the marine resources around Pag-asa Island and the Kalayaan Island Group. This mission is in accordance with the guidance of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., who has called for firm national resolve in defending what is ours and for responsible stewardship of the country's marine resources.— Jay Tarriela (@jaytaryela) October 4, 2026

The PCG said the China Coast Guard had "no law enforcement authority" in the territorial sea of Pag-asa and said its actions "made it easier for a suspected violator to escape." It also rejected any Chinese claim that its vessels had been expelled from the area.

At just 37 hectares (0.14 square miles), the coral-fringed Pag-asa is the largest and most prized of the nine Philippines-held features in the Spratly archipelago, located 450 km (280 miles) from the mainland.

Separately, the military said a Chinese J-16 fighter jet repeatedly approached and maneuvered close to a Philippine patrol aircraft over the disputed Scarborough Shoal on Saturday, creating an aviation safety risk.
The Armed Forces of the Philippines said the incident was part of a "recurring pattern of unsafe and coercive behavior" against Philippine vessels and aircraft conducting lawful operations.
The Chinese Embassy in Manila did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the weekend incidents. — Reuters

articles.title: [Inside the Newsroom] Mary Jane Veloso made us cry and realize why we want to be journalists
articles.summary: Our reporters followed Mary Jane Veloso for 48 hours — from her release from prison to her homecoming in Nueva Ecija

blocks.text: September 25 was supposed to be a normal Friday work day, until President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. announced in an interview: he has pardoned former overseas worker Mary Jane Velasco.
I alerted my desk editors, broke the story, and triggered Rappler’s 48-hour coverage of Veloso’s release and freedom.
Hello! This is justice reporter Jairo Bolledo.

I broke down in tears as I was choosing a display photo for the story on Veloso’s pardon. I picked a 2024 photograph where she was crying and talking to her family via video call. It was taken on the day of her return to the Philippines.
I knew it was going to be a long weekend ahead of us. At any moment, Veloso would be released from the Correctional Institution for Women (CIW) in Mandaluyong City.

While waiting for updates in the afternoon, I wrote, shot, and edited a video explainer on Veloso’s case. In the early evening, as I headed for dinner with colleagues, a Bureau of Corrections (BuCor) official announced that Veloso would be released that night — at 8 pm.
Because all Rappler cars were out on other coverages, head of news operations Acor Arceo drove me and fellow reporter Jelo Ritzhie Mantaring to CIW. We arrived a few minutes before 8 pm.
There was a table set up inside the CIW’s holding area. The last time I was in that room was when I covered Veloso’s transfer from Indonesia to the Philippines.
At past 8:30 pm, a smiling Veloso — dressed in white shirt and gray sweatpants — entered the room. She was beaming the whole time. She was a different Veloso.
I learned about her case in 2015 as a freshman journalism student. I pictured her as a woman who was always worried and timid. She was on death row at the time.

Nine years later, in 2024, I covered her return as a reporter. I saw a happy Veloso. Then on September 25, 2026, I had the ultimate privilege of covering her release. I witnessed a truly free Mary Jane.

After a short press conference with BuCor Director General Gregorio Catapang Jr., Veloso stayed with her lawyers from the National Union of Peoples’ Lawyers and advocates from Migrante International, who had seen her case through.

I approached the groups and asked if I could get 15 minutes of Veloso’s time for a Rappler Talk interview. The groups said yes. Veloso enthusiastically accepted my offer. It was her first exclusive and sit-down interview since her pardon.

blocks.caption: [Inside the Newsroom] Mary Jane Veloso made us cry and realize why we want to be journalists

blocks.text: I talked to Veloso as if we were long-time acquaintances. I held back tears while listening to her story about her life in prison, her plans for her family, and how she feels about the people who had wronged her.

blocks.caption: WITH MARY JANE. A photo with Mary Jane Veloso after the Rappler Talk interview on September 25, 2026.

blocks.text: That was one of the most important interviews I had ever done in my career. It was a coverage of a lifetime.
Afterwards, I tried shaking Veloso’s hands, but she hugged me instead. She is warm. She is grateful. She still is a cheerful person after all the hurdles she had faced.
We stayed in CIW to cover her reunion with family. We followed the family until their transfer from CIW to a hotel in Manila in the early hours of September 26.
Veloso’s story is one of those that makes us realize why we do what we do. Why we chose journalism. Why we chose public service.

blocks.caption: [Inside the Newsroom] Rappler was built for stories like Mary Jane Veloso’s

blocks.text: It’s not every day that we win in our crusade for a better world or against the atrocities. Veloso’s freedom after 16 years is a win for everyone — for herself, her family, and for all the people who have been helping her in the last 16 years.

blocks.caption: RAPPLER TEAM FOR VELOSO. Production specialist Jon Vic Digma (most left); assistant production specialist and driver Ramil Cedeño (upper center); reporter Jelo Ritzhie Mantaring (lower center); and Jairo Bolledo (most right).

blocks.text: That’s why Veloso’s journey back home to Nueva Ecija was also part of the wins that must be documented.
Hi! Jelo Ritzhie Mantaring here. I report about social issues, including migration and overseas Filipino workers (OFWs).

I met Mary Jane Veloso again at the Siena College Chapel in Quezon City at 9:40 am on Saturday, September 26. She was attending Mass — her first activity as a free woman. While waiting for the Mass, I asked her how she slept after her release from the CIW.

“Hindi po ako makatulog. Ito po, namamaga ang mata ko. Pasens’ya na po, siguro masyado akong nao-overwhelm sa pamilya, sa lahat ng sumusuporta,” she said. (I cannot sleep. Look, that’s why I have puffy eyes. I’m sorry, maybe I’m too overwhelmed with my family and all those who are supporting me.)
Later, I would learn from her sister, Maritess Laurente, that Veloso gets carsick easily. It was Darling Cando, the closest sibling to Veloso, who made sure that they would bring Bonamine for her.

It was surreal for me that Veloso decided to attend Mass and hold a news conference first before traveling for hours to her home province with lack of sleep. I thought, her will and determination to give thanks to God and supporters were unmatched.
I interviewed her siblings to learn more about the family she came from. And this is what I saw: love was patient and overflowing between them.
At 3 pm, the Veloso family began their trip to Nueva Ecija. Our team went ahead of them.

blocks.caption: HOMECOMING. The family of Mary Jane Veloso set up a simple celebration for the return of the former overseas Filipino worker in General Mamerto Natividad, Nueva Ecija, on September 26, 2026. Photo by Jelo Ritzhie Mantaring/Rappler

blocks.text: Upon arriving in General Mamerto Natividad town, we saw some tables and chairs set up. There were homecoming banners, small balloons, and a crowd of relatives and neighbors. She arrived — finally home — at 5:43 pm.
I knew I was there to cover. But I also remember asking myself: Why, really, am I here?

The answer came during their dinner. Veloso, happily eating her requested pinakbet and inihaw na tilapia, was surrounded by her family. The Veloso family, complete. I took a video of that moment, not as a way of intruding into their family, but to help announce that Mary Jane was home at last and will be starting life anew.
This, ultimately, is the journalism I want to keep doing: the one that puts the spotlight on ordinary families, and where they are in the policies and systems that the powerful create for them.

Like Mary Jane Veloso, many Filipinos may also be risking everything to provide for their families. And they are taken advantage of because of that vulnerability. Her documented cautionary tale must push the government to better protect our countrymen.
That’s where journalism helps. And you, too, join us in this mission when you decide to support the journalism that Rappler does.

blocks.caption: VELOSO BACK HOME. Rappler reporter Jelo Ritzhie Mantaring recaps the coverage of Mary Jane Veloso’s trip back home to General Mamerto Natividad, Nueva Ecija, on September 26, 2026. Photo by Jon Vic Digma/Rappler

articles.title: PH military says ‘close encounter’ with China fighter plane near Bajo de Masinloc
articles.summary: Two Chinese planes, including a J-16 fighter aircraft, had a 'close encounter' with a Philippine military plane

blocks.text: BLOCKED. A satellite image of fishing vessels at the entrance, which is blocked by a floating barrier, to the disputed Scarborough Shoal, in the South China Sea, April 11, 2026.
Vantor/Handout via Reuters
Two Chinese planes, including a J-16 fighter aircraft, had a 'close encounter' with a Philippine military plane

items: The Armed Forces of the Philippines confirmed a close encounter between a military plane and a Chinese J-16 fighter during a maritime patrol near Bajo de Masinloc on October 3.
The AFP stated that the Chinese aircraft's maneuvers posed aviation safety risks and highlighted a pattern of unsafe behavior against Philippine vessels and aircraft in the area.
Bajo de Masinloc is within the Philippines' exclusive economic zone but has been controlled by China since 2012, leading to ongoing tensions between the two countries over sovereignty claims.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines — The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Sunday, October 4, confirmed a “close encounter” between a small military plane and two Chinese aircraft, including what they confirmed was a J-16 fighter aircraft, during an October 3 maritime patrol in the vicinity of Bajo de Masinloc.

In a statement Sunday afternoon, the AFP said one of its C-208 aircraft was conducting a maritime patrol in the vicinity of Bajo de Masinloc or Scarborough Shoal when the J-16 fighter plane “repeatedly approached and maneuvered in close proximity to the Philippine aircraft, including maneuvering ahead of and around it and positioning itself within the Philippine aircraft’s wake.”
“These maneuvers posed an aviation safety risk,” said the AFP.

“This incident is part of a recurring pattern of unsafe and coercive behavior against Philippine government vessels and aircraft conducting lawful operations. The AFP will continue to document and expose such actions that place Philippine personnel and assets at unnecessary risk,” said the military.

Bajo de Masinloc is a high-tide elevation just over 124 nautical miles from Zambales, a province in Luzon. While it is within the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone (EEZ), access to the shoal has been controlled by China since 2012, following a standoff between Manila and Beijing. The two countries claim sovereignty over the shoal.

Controlling the shoal has meant that out at sea, Chinese maritime forces routinely harass Philippine vessels and aircraft that approach Bajo de Masinloc. Similar incidents have happened to Philippine government vessels and aircraft belonging to its civilian maritime agencies.

No casualties were reported from the incident and the Philippine plane still completed its mission. “The AFP will continue to conduct routine maritime and air patrols in the West Philippine Sea. The AFP remains vigilant and will continue to prioritize the safety of its personnel and aircraft while carrying out its mandate,” added the AFP.

Bilateral ties between the Philippines and China have mostly been tense since 2012 over disputes in the West Philippine Sea, a portion of the South China Sea that includes the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone.

In 2016, the Philippines won a landmark Arbitral Award that affirmed its EEZ in the West Philippine Sea and deemed China’s supposed historical claim over the South China Sea invalid. Beijing does not recognize the decision.

The tribunal could not determine sovereignty claims, including over features like Bajo de Masinloc. It did, however, say that since the shoal was a historical fishing ground for Filipino, Chinese, Vietnamese, and Taiwanese fisherfolk, small-scale fishing should not be impeded, no matter who has sovereignty over the shoal. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Cornell president calls alleged gang rape 'deeply disturbing,' pledges greater transparency
articles.summary: Scrutiny has mounted in recent days over Cornell's response to allegations that the woman was sexually assaulted by multiple fraternity members in 2024. The woman, identified in court documents as…

image.caption: Pedestrians walk on the campus at Cornell University in Ithaca, N.Y., Thursday, Oct. 1, 2026. (Matt Rourke/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

Scrutiny has mounted in recent days over Cornell's response to allegations that the woman was sexually assaulted by multiple fraternity members in 2024. The woman, identified in court documents as Jane Doe, has sued the university and seven former students.
Michael Kotlikoff addressed the Cornell community in an 8-minute video message

Cornell's president called the alleged gang rape of a student at a fraternity house in 2024 "deeply disturbing" Saturday, said it would weigh on the university for years to come and pledged greater transparency amid mounting outrage over the school's handling of the case.

In an eight-minute video message to the Cornell community, Michael Kotlikoff described the past week as one of the most difficult in the university's history and acknowledged troubling questions about the investigations that followed the allegations.

items: What Cornell's alleged rape case and the Hockey Canada trial's striking parallels reveal

blocks.text: "My heart aches when I think of what she experienced," Kotlikoff said. "It raises heartbreaking and troubling issues about sexual assault, dehumanization and aspects of party culture, alcohol and drug use."

Kotlikoff reaffirmed his commitment to supporting an independent review of Cornell's handling of the case called for by New York Gov. Kathy Hochul and said the school's Board of Trustees would announce details next week. He also expressed support for Hochul's decision to turn the criminal investigation over to the state attorney general.
N.Y. governor appoints special prosecutor to Cornell sexual assault case

"I want to acknowledge something that can be difficult for an institution to say," Kotlikoff said. "We don't have all the answers, but we are committed to investigating and finding the answers our community deserves."

During a student assembly hearing Thursday that gave students an opportunity to voice concerns and discuss proposals to improve Cornell's response to sexual assault, several speakers called for Kotlikoff's resignation.

items: 'I am Jane Doe': Online rally to protect Cornell rape accuser's identity becomes a reckoning

blocks.text: Hochul, asked at a news conference Friday whether she believed Kotlikoff should resign over the university's handling of the case, declined to take a position, saying she did not yet have enough information.

Kotlikoff acknowledged frustration that Cornell has not communicated enough, saying that has led to distrust. While citing "real legal and privacy limits" on what the university can disclose, he pledged greater transparency and more opportunities for students, parents and others to engage with university leaders.
Student journalists demand answers in ‘Cornell 7’ case
He also committed Cornell's support to legislative efforts to change New York's sexual assault laws.

The case has renewed scrutiny of a state law that makes it difficult to prosecute sexual assaults involving people who voluntarily consume alcohol or drugs, even if they became too intoxicated to consent.

items: Cornell 7: Governor vows to change N.Y. rape law that makes reporting hard when intoxication present

blocks.text: Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten cited the law in defending his initial decision not to pursue charges, saying the woman's original statement to police described voluntary drug use and sexual activity.

Critics have long sought to close what they call the "voluntary intoxication loophole," which distinguishes between people incapacitated by drugs administered without their consent and those who voluntarily became intoxicated. Hochul has pledged to push for changes to the law.

Kotlikoff also called for a "serious look at the role of fraternities and sororities in campus life," saying Cornell would engage students, alumni and others in examining how to preserve the benefits of Greek life while strengthening accountability and transparency.
"Being part of a group can never diminish individual responsibility for our own actions, for how we treat others or for speaking up when someone may be at risk," he said.

articles.title: Danggit, mangroves tell story of coastal recovery in Prieto Diaz, Sorsogon
articles.summary: Once facing severe decline, the 1,000-hectare Prieto Diaz mangrove forest in Sorsogon has been transformed by local residents into a thriving, community-managed sanctuary that protects both their…

blocks.text: MAJESTIC. Local guides and paddlers bring tourists to the famed 'bakawan' of Prieto Diaz, Sorsogon.
Marky Ramone Go

Once facing severe decline, the 1,000-hectare Prieto Diaz mangrove forest in Sorsogon has been transformed by local residents into a thriving, community-managed sanctuary that protects both their livelihoods and the coastline

items: Prieto Diaz, Sorsogon has successfully rehabilitated its coastal ecosystem, particularly its mangrove forests, through community-led efforts since 1993.
The formation of the community organization SEAMANCOR has played a crucial role in managing and protecting the mangroves, which are vital for local livelihoods and biodiversity.

The community's commitment to conservation has led to national recognition and sustainable tourism development, highlighting the importance of the mangrove ecosystem for both the environment and the local economy.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

In Prieto Diaz, Sorsogon, danggit is more than a local delicacy. The rabbitfish that become the town’s dried fish thrive in nearly 1,000 hectares of seagrass meadows, part of a larger coastal ecosystem of seagrass, coral reefs, and mangroves that supports both the town’s livelihood and its marine life.

At the center of Prieto Diaz’s coastal conservation story is an ecosystem that has not always been this healthy. After decades of community-led protection, the town’s coastal habitats have recovered. Today, its mangrove forest spans more than 1,000 hectares, making it one of the largest community-managed mangrove forests in the Bicol region.

blocks.caption: A Prieto Diaz local paddles his way through the mangrove forest. All photos by Marky Ramone Go

blocks.text: The transformation began in 1993, when the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) selected Prieto Diaz as a pilot site for a coastal rehabilitation project. The program eventually led to the formation of Seagrass, Mangrove, Corals (SEAMANCOR), a community organization whose members became bantay dagat (sea patrol), mangrove wardens, and guides for visitors.
The recovery also involved people who patrol the waters, guide visitors through the bakawan, the Tagalog word for mangroves, and monitor the coastal ecosystem.

For Victor Emata, a paddler and guide, that work started when he began seeing the mangroves return. He remembers the early rehabilitation efforts in the 1990s, led by the DENR in partnership with the Agta-Tabangnon community and other organizations across the barangays.

“Through the protection of the mangroves, we are able to preserve the different mangrove species that can thrive here, as well as the other species like different birds, that depend on the mangrove ecosystem,” he said in Filipino.
As the forest recovered, visitors began arriving, and Victor became one of the paddlers and guides introducing them to the bakawan.
For Montano Eva Jr., protecting the restored mangroves meant enforcing the rules. When fishing restrictions were introduced, community members organized sea patrols.
Some violators were caught and fined, and Montano says the number of fishermen operating inside the protected area eventually declined. Today, residents continue taking turns guarding the mangroves.

blocks.caption: An aerial view of over 1,000 hectares of mangrove forests in Prieto Diaz, Sorsogon.

blocks.text: Manuel Domdom, a fisherman, guide and president of the local guides’ organization, says the bakawan has become a big part of the community’s daily life.

“The bakawan is an important source of income for the fishermen in our community,” he said. “For those of us who live here in Prieto Diaz, we believe the bakawan is also a blessing from God. That is why we feel a responsibility to preserve it for our town and for our people.”
That responsibility is not always easy. Manuel says some people still attempt to cut or collect trees despite regulations, while the area remains an important fishing ground.
For Manuel, protecting the bakawan also means protecting the community’s fishing livelihood and the coast itself from storm surges.
Restoration eventually gave way to a system of community management and, later, tourism.

According to Oriculo Despuig Jr., the municipality’s tourism officer-designate, the process began when DENR assessed the condition of the mangrove forest and worked with an indigenous peoples group. Members were encouraged to plant mangrove propagules in designated areas in exchange for payment.

This was followed by the formation of SEAMANCOR in 1994, a community-based organization composed largely of fishermen and their wives. DENR eventually awarded the group a 25-year Mangrove Stewardship Agreement, formalizing its role in managing and protecting the restored forest.

Mangroves had been cut for charcoal and firewood, with some sold to nearby bakeries and others used by fishermen for fishpen construction. Illegal fishing, including the use of dynamite and poisonous substances, also threatened the coastal ecosystem.
The bantay dagat helped enforce the rules. Some fishermen were later trained as boat paddlers and guides for the community’s Mangrove Tours.
“Now the community, especially the coastal barangays, is aware that DENR regulations pertaining to mangroves are being implemented, especially for their protection and preservation,” says Despuig.

The community’s work eventually earned national recognition. The municipality was named the 2020 national grand winner of the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources’ (BFAR) Malinis at Masaganang Karagatan (MMK) program, receiving P30-million worth of fisheries livelihood projects. The incentive-based program recognizes communities for stronger coastal governance and sustainable marine resource management.

blocks.caption: The lush fauna in the Prieto Diaz mangroves in Sorsogon.

blocks.text: Despuig hopes the mangrove forest will continue expanding over the next five to 10 years, eventually stretching from the poblacion toward Barangay Talisayan and the boundary with Sorsogon City.
For Fatit Guttierez Bayle, Prieto Diaz’s tourism officer, the future of the mangrove forest is personal.

Bayle said she chose to build her career in her hometown rather than pursue an opportunity with the United Nations: “As (Prieto Diaz’s) tourism officer, I did not give up a bigger life because I found a better one.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: PH nets biggest Asian Games medal haul in 6 decades
articles.summary: Gymnastics star Carlos Yulo, pole vault stalwart EJ Obiena, and taekwondo standout Jeus Yape show the way for the Philippines' 29-medal finish in the 2026 Asian Games

blocks.text: DELIVER. Carlos Yulo, EJ Obiena, and Jeus Yape banner the Philippines' medalists in the 2026 Asian Games.
PSC-POC Media Pool and Reuters
Gymnastics star Carlos Yulo, pole vault stalwart EJ Obiena, and taekwondo standout Jeus Yape show the way for the Philippines' 29-medal finish in the 2026 Asian Games

items: The Philippines achieved its largest medal haul at the Asian Games in 60 years, finishing with 29 medals: 4 golds, 9 silvers, and 16 bronzes.

Gymnast Carlos Yulo led the team with two gold medals, while EJ Obiena and Jeus Gabriel Derick Yape contributed one gold each, marking significant achievements in gymnastics, pole vault, and taekwondo.
Despite falling short of their target of eight golds, the Philippines equaled its previous gold medal counts from the 2023 and 2018 editions, while China dominated the overall medal standings.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – The Philippines recorded its biggest Asian Games haul in six decades as it wrapped up its campaign in the 20th edition in Nagoya, Japan, on Sunday, October 4, with four golds, nine silvers, and 16 bronzes for a total of 29 medals.
Although the country matched its 17th-place finish in 2023 in Hangzhou, China, it came away with its most medals since winning 42 in the 1966 staging in Bangkok, Thailand.

Gymnastics star Carlos Yulo showed the way for the delegation with two golds, while pole vault stalwart EJ Obiena and taekwondo standout Jeus Gabriel Derick Yape scored one each as they all claimed a piece of history.

Yulo ruled in men’s floor exercise and vault — the same events in which he captured his two Olympics golds — to become the first Filipino gymnast to win an Asian Games medal. In doing so, he completed his collection which includes titles from the World Championships, Asian Championships, World Cup, and Southeast Asian Games.
Obiena defended his men’s pole vault crown in record-breaking fashion, setting a new Asian Games mark of 5.91 meters as he emerged as only the fourth back-to-back champion in the event.

Then in a breakthrough in taekwondo, Yape became the Philippines’ first-ever Asian Games gold medalist in the sport following his triumph in the mixed individual virtual taekwondo, an event that debuted in the continental showpiece.
Yape secured the landmark gold for Philippine taekwondo after bagging bronze in the men’s individual poomsae.
With four golds, the country equaled its tally in 2023 and 2018 in Jakarta-Palembang, Indonesia.

The Philippine Olympic Committee and Philippine Sports Commission initially set an eight-gold target — a haul that, if achieved, would have marked the Philippines’ first time winning at least five golds in a single edition since its seven-gold showing in 1962.
But a fifth gold remained elusive, with the country enduring final losses in mixed martial arts, 3×3 basketball, sepak takraw, archery, boxing, taekwondo, and jiu-jitsu.

MMA fighter Jean Claude Saclag (men’s traditional -65kg) delivered the first silver followed by the Gilas Women team of Kacey dela Rosa, Kennan Ka, Amyah Espanol, and Maria Pasilang (women’s 3×3 basketball), the sepak takraw squad of Jean Marie Sucalit, Abegail Sinogbuhan, and Nelly Jay Salon (women’s double), archer Amaya Amparo Cojuangco (women’s individual compound), and taekwondo jin Juliana Mykhail Candelaria (women’s individual poomsae).

The Philippines stayed on track to break through that four-gold ceiling on Friday, October 2, as boxer Carlo Paalam (men’s 55kg) and taekwondo bets Tachiana Mangin (women’s -49kg) and Kurt Barbosa (men’s -58kg) all reached the finals, only to fall short in their respective title bouts.

Jiu-jitsu champion Alexandria Enriquez (women’s -63kg) stood as the Philippines’ last hope for a fifth gold on Saturday, October 3, but she suffered the same fate as Paalam, Mangin, and Barbosa following a narrow loss by advantage to Thailand’s Orapa Senatham.

The Philippines secured 16 bronzes, its most since also bagging 16 in 2002, with the likes of tennis star Alex Eala (women’s singles), gymnast Eldrew Yulo (men’s horizontal bar), weightlifter Albert Ian delos Santos (men’s 70kg), and athletics bets Victoria Bossong (women’s 800m) and John Cabang Tolentino (men’s 110m hurdles) also contributing to the tally.
As expected, China claimed the overall championship, doing so for the 12th consecutive edition as it dominated with 169 golds, 89 silvers, and 83 bronzes.
Host Japan finished second in the medal standings for the third straight time with 83 golds, 95 silvers, and 91 bronzes, while South Korea placed third with 39 golds, 43 silvers, and 68 bronzes.

Meanwhile, Thailand ended up as the best Southeast Asian nation, landing at seventh with 18 golds, 13 silvers, and 21 bronzes followed by Malaysia (9-7-16) at 11th, Indonesia (5-11-23) at 16th, then the Philippines.

articles.summary:
Moscow struck city’s North Bridge this morning, around 20-minutes drive away from the station where the German chancellor arrived

The North Bridge – one of several connecting central…

blocks.text: Key events

items: 7m agoAttack on Kyiv as Merz arrives shows upsurge in Russian attacks on capital
22m agoOpening summary

blocks.text: Merz has met Ukraine’s President Voldymyr Zelenskyy at the main war memorial on the Maidan in Kyiv.

Both men lay tributes at the central site, which features thousands of Ukrainian flags and framed portraits of the soldiers who’ve been killed in the war that’s gone on for more than four-and-a-half years.
Some pictures from the scene just now:

blocks.caption: Merz and Zelenskyy pay tribute at the makeshift memorial to fallen Ukrainian defenders at the Independence Square in Kyiv, Ukraine, October 4, 2026. REUTERS/Alina Smutko Photograph: Alina Smutko/Reuters

blocks.text: Attack on Kyiv as Merz arrives shows upsurge in Russian attacks on capital

The North Bridge – one of several connecting central historic Kyiv to the residential suburbs across the Dnipro river -was struck not long after the German chancellor’s arrival in the Ukrainian capital.
The incident has been confirmed by Kyiv’s mayor Vitali Klitschko this morning who wrote on Telegram: “Impact on the road surface of the Northern Bridge. Emergency services are heading to the scene.”
There’s no word of casualties yet. Pictures and footage being shared online appears to show a missile slamming into the cable bridge and the resulting fireball explosion.
It follows strikes by the Russians on the South Bridge on Friday and Saturday, and several earlier this week that had shut three of the city’s six road bridges over the Dnipro.
Merz has arrived in the thick of it, as Kyiv, which was largely spared direct aerial strikes in the first years of the war has increasingly come under attack since April.
The Russians have launched strikes day and night, hitting schools, petrol strations, government buildings and churches as well as rails and communication infrastructure.
Opening summary
Good morning and welcome to our Europe live blog, I’m Frances Mao.
We begin in Kyiv where one of Ukraine’s strongest European backers, the German chancellor Friedrich Merz, has arrived this morning in an unannounced visit.
Soon after his arrival, the Russians struck the city’s North Bridge, just a 20-minutes drive from the central railway station where Merz had pulled into.

Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro face off in battle between leftwing incumbent and far-right son of jailed ex-president

Brazilians go to the polls on Sunday in the first round of a highly polarised…
articles.byline: Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro

blocks.text: Brazilians go to the polls on Sunday in the first round of a highly polarised and high-stakes presidential election that could change not only the direction of Latin America’s largest country but that of the entire region.

The election pits the leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who is seeking a fourth non-consecutive term, against the far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, an ally of Donald Trump and the son of the former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year sentence for attempting a coup after his failed 2022 re-election attempt.

Brazil is one of the few Latin American countries that still has a leftwing government after a wave of rightwing and far-right electoral victories across the region and the US takeover of Venezuela following the capture of Nicolás Maduro.

blocks.caption: Lula parading through São Paulo on Saturday. Photograph: Sebastião Moreira/EPA

blocks.text: The 80-year-old Lula has positioned himself as one of the last regional leaders still willing to say no to Trump, and has recently accused the US president of trying to interfere in Brazil’s election in Bolsonaro’s favour.

Like his father, who was Brazil’s president during Trump’s first term, Flávio Bolsonaro, 45, frequently praises the US president and has pledged to join the US-led anti-drug cartel coalition that has killed dozens in airstrikes and carried out military operations across the region.

Lula and Bolsonaro have alternated as frontrunners in the final stretch, making the outcome unpredictable. In recent days, both have focused on persuading undecided voters in hopes of reaching 50% plus one vote; if neither does, there will be a runoff on 25 October.

“My first choice would be Jair Bolsonaro but, since he is under house arrest and there is no other rightwing candidate strong enough to take on the current president, I’m going with Flávio,” said Claudinei Ferreira Viana, 45, a workshop manager in Pinhais, in Paraná state.

At the beginning of the year, polls suggested Bolsonaro voters would have preferred a ticket led by the São Paulo governor, Tarcísio de Freitas, or the former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro. But the former president chose his eldest son.

The campaign was also marked by a scandal in which the senator was caught on tape asking a banker accused of corruption for $26.8m (£20m) to fund a film about his father, as well as speculation that Bolsonaro might strip the country’s widely cherished patron saint of her status, but he has nevertheless remained highly competitive.

blocks.caption: Flávio Bolsonaro during an open-top campaign parade through the Campo Grande district of Rio de Janeiro on Saturday. Photograph: Bruna Prado/AP

blocks.text: For many analysts, that reflects a combination of a straightforward transfer of his father’s voter base – Jair Bolsonaro lost to Lula by less than two percentage points in 2022 – and an anti-Lula vote, with the president still facing high rejection rates despite strong social and economic indicators.

The incumbent’s campaign has also been hit by corruption allegations – still under investigation – involving his son and a former aide, as well as a scandal involving supreme court justices which, despite having no connection to Lula, is seen as fuelling an “anti-system” vote and, by extension, an anti-incumbent one.
Brazilians will also elect 27 state governors, members of state legislatures, all 513 federal congress members and 54 of the country’s 81 senators in Sunday’s vote.

AMC, 40, who asked to be identified only by her initials because she fears reprisals from the local conservative government where she works in the interior of Amazonas state, will vote for Lula on Sunday “because of the many programmes he created to support the most vulnerable groups”.

“Jair Bolsonaro weakened protections for Indigenous peoples, and everything Lula has done over the past four years to strengthen those protections and protect the Amazon would be seriously threatened if his son came to power,” she said.

articles.title: India news: Police order probe amid sexual harassment allegations against officers at Delhi protest
articles.summary: Three women journalists say police officers sexually harassed them as they covered protests demanding the resignation of India's election chief. Meanwhile, LGBTQIA influencer Mad Sandhu was shot dead…

image.caption: Scores of protesters were detained at Jantar Mantar on Saturday Image: ANI/IMAGO

blocks.text: October 4, 2026
Police order probe amid sexual harassment allegations against officers at Delhi protest

blocks.caption: Delhi Police personnel are facing allegations of harassment during the Saturday protest at Jantar MantarImage: ANI/IMAGO

blocks.text: Delhi Police have begun an inquiry into complaints by three women journalists who say they were sexually harassed by police personnel while covering protests against India's chief election commissioner.
In a statement on social media, police said the complaints were referred to the Crime Branch for a "fair and impartial enquiry."

The allegations emerged as police detained protesters near New Delhi's Jantar Mantar for a second day on Saturday, after over 700 people were detained on Friday. Demonstrators have been demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a mass voter-roll revision that has removed millions of names. The commission denies wrongdoing.
Kumar has not publicly commented.

In a video shared by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke, one journalist alleged that an assistant commissioner of police groped her while she filmed the detention of student activist Neha Bora. Police have not publicly responded to the specific allegation.
Journalists and protesters gathered outside the Parliament Street police station demanding a report be filed, local media reported.

The Press Club of India expressed "shock and dismay" at the treatment of journalists and urged swift action. Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi asked Home Minister Amit Shah to respond, noting that Delhi Police fall under his ministry.
Several student groups have called for a march from India Gate to Jantar Mantar on Sunday at 3 p.m. local time.
Meanwhile, opposition parties plan to march on the Election Commission on Tuesday, and the CJP has called for a mass mobilization in Delhi on October 10.

articles.title: Kyiv bridge hit in further drone attack as German chancellor makes surprise visit
articles.summary: Unverified video shows a drone hitting the Northern Bridge as vehicles move across it.

blocks.text: A major bridge in Kyiv has been targeted by Russian strikes for the second day in a row, coinciding with a surprise visit from German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's to the city.
The Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge was hit on Sunday morning, a day after it was first struck by drones in an attack that damaged the road surface and led to traffic disruption.
Kyiv Major Vitali Klitschko said Sunday's strike had also damaged a heating main, adding that there would be a temporary lack of hot water in the north-eastern Desnyanskyi district as a result.
Major bridges have been targeted in Kyiv over the past four days as Moscow ramps up attacks on critical infrastructure in the capital.

Unverified video footage of Sunday's strike shows cars moving on the bridge as a drone crashes into it before exploding, creating a ball of fire. A cloud of black smoke can be seen rising above the bridge.
Klitschko reported the strike on Telegram, writing: "Hitting the roadway on the North Bridge. Emergency services are on their way to the scene."
As emergency services responded to the incident, Germany's Merz reaffirmed his country's support for Ukraine and pledged further assistance to bolster Ukrainian air defences.
He wrote on X: "Ukraine is facing decisive weeks. That is why I travelled to Kyiv today with the message: You can rely on us.
"Germany's security also depends on the outcome of this war. That is why we are helping out of our own self-interest as well."

articles.title: Palace leaves prosecution to decide on bribery allegations vs Sara Duterte
articles.summary: Malacañang on Sunday said it would leave it to the House prosecution team to decide whether to drop the bribery allegations against Vice President Sara Duterte in her impeachment case, but warned…

blocks.text: Published October 4, 2026 4:18pm

Malacañang on Sunday said it would leave it to the House prosecution team to decide whether to drop the bribery allegations against Vice President Sara Duterte in her impeachment case, but warned that doing so could leave Filipinos without answers.

“Nasa pagpapasya po iyan ng prosecution. Kung sa tingin nila ay iyan ang tamang strategy sa paghahain ng mga testigo. Ngunit isinama nila iyan sa Articles of Impeachment, na ang ibig sabihin nito ay may sapat silang ebidensya para talakayin itong isyung bribery sa impeachment court,” Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said.

(That is up to the prosecution to decide. If they believe that is the right strategy in presenting their witnesses. But they included it in the Articles of Impeachment, which means they have sufficient evidence to raise the bribery issue before the impeachment court.)
Castro, however, reminded the prosecution that dropping the bribery allegations could deprive Filipinos of the opportunity to know the full truth about the matter.

“Kung aatras sila sa akusasyong bribery laban sa Bise Presidente, hindi ba nila nasi-shortchange o nadedehado ang mga Filipino na nais sanang malaman ang buong katotohanan rito? Muli, nasa kanila po ang pagpapasya rito,” she added.

(If they withdraw the bribery allegations against the Vice President, wouldn’t they be shortchanging or disadvantaging Filipinos who want to know the full truth about the matter? Again, the decision is up to them.)

In a Super Radyo dzBB interview, House prosecution spokesperson and Lanao del Sur 1st District Representative Zia Alonto Adiong said the prosecution team was likely to drop the bribery allegations against Duterte.

“Mukhang ang direction is hindi na siya ita-tackle. Maybe that's the direction, pero hindi pa natin pina-finalize 'yan kasi ongoing pa rin ang discussion sa prosecution panel kung anong magiging susunod na hakbang pagkatapos ng Article 2,” Adiong told Super Radyo dzBB.

(It appears that it will no longer be tackled. That may be the direction, but we have not finalized it yet because discussions are still ongoing among the prosecution panel on what the next steps will be after Article 2.)
Asked whether the possible decision was because the first three impeachment articles were already strong enough to convict Duterte, Adiong said this was the case.
The Senate Impeachment Court is currently hearing Article 2 of the Articles of Impeachment, which accuses Duterte of unexplained wealth.
Article 3, meanwhile, accuses the Vice President of bribing officials of the Department of Education during her stint as DepEd secretary from 2022 to 2024.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Germany's Merz visits Kyiv as Russia strikes bridge
articles.summary: A Kyiv bridge was hit by a Russian drone shortly after Chancellor Merz arrived in the Ukrainian capital. During his visit, Merz is set to announce new measures to support Ukraine, including plans for…

image.caption: Friedrich Merz joined Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in paying tribute to fallen Ukrainian soldiersImage: Kay Nietfeld/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv, on Sunday morning, accompanied by Economy Minister Katherina Reiche and a delegation of leading German economic figures.
"If Russia is not stopped, it will turn its war machine against us sooner or later," Merz said upon his arrival by train.
Air raid sirens blared across the Ukrainian capital throughout the morning, as Kyiv's mayor announced one of the city's bridges had been hit by a Russian drone.

During his visit, Merz is expected to announce a new raft of measures to support Ukraine in its fight against the ongoing Russian invasion, including a further billion euros in German military aid, plus €350 million ($395 million) for energy sector repairs, according to German media reports.
The chancellor is also expected to unveil plans for the co-production of interceptor drones and long-range missiles both in Ukraine and Germany.

blocks.caption: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in Kyiv by train on Sunday morningImage: Kay Nietfeld/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Focus on ramping up drone production

According to German government sources cited by the Reuters and dpa news agencies, arms production is expected to focus on the development and delivery of thousands of drones capable of intercepting the rapid, jet-powered drones increasingly being deployed by the Russian military against civilian infrastructure targets in Ukraine.

The production of missiles with a range of over 1,000 kilometers (620 miles) is also expected to be ramped up, enhancing Ukraine's ability to strike military and logistical targets far beyond the frontline and inside Russia itself.
Merz is expected to emphasize how Germany also stands to benefit from the expanded cooperation, both in terms of its own defense against Russian hybrid activities and in terms of jobs and technology.
The chancellor is also expected to speak to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy about the progress of political reforms in Ukraine and the continuing battle against corruption.
Can Ukraine still count on Germany?
Russia strikes Kyiv bridge during Merz visit
The visit comes just hours after the Russian Foreign Ministry warned foreign diplomats and other visitors to avoid the Ukrainian capital, and military and government buildings in particular.

"The responsibility for any negative consequences lies entirely with those who ignore this warning," read a statement, which claimed that Russian strikes were responses to "terrorist acts by the Ukrainian armed forces against our country's civilian infrastructure."

In recent days, Russia has attacked several bridges across the Dnipro river as well as energy infrastructure, and the city's mayor, Vitali Klitschko, on Friday said that Kyiv was in a "very dramatic situation."
Another strike followed on Sunday during Merz's visit, with Klitschko confirming that a bridge had been struck.
"Impact on the road surface of the Northern Bridge. Emergency services are heading to the scene," the mayor wrote on the Telegram messaging service.
But the German delegation has not been deterred, with Merz saying upon arrival that "Ukraine will need all our support in the coming weeks" as winter approaches and Russian attacks intensify.
"A fifth winter of war is about to begin," he said. "Russia is bombarding cities, apartments and power stations. I will tell President Zelenskyy today: 'You can count on our help.'"
Russia targets Kyiv bridge network
Merz: 'If Germany wavers, Ukraine wavers'
Merz's arrival in Kyiv marks the fourth such visit to Ukraine by a German chancellor since the full-scale Russian invasion began in February 2022.

His predecessor, Olaf Scholz, visited twice during his three-year tenure, while Merz himself first traveled to Kyiv in May 2025 – just four days after taking office. He was accompanied on that occasion by French President Emmanuel Macron, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk and former British Prime Minister Keir Starmer.
Sunday's visit comes just days after Merz had assured Ukraine of Germany's support, despite isolated resistance and criticism at home.

"If we in Germany waver, Europe wavers," he said on Thursday after conferring the international Westphalian Peace Prize upon the NATO military alliance and its secretary general, Mark Rutte. "And if Europe wavers, Ukraine wavers."

Germany remains Ukraine's most important backer, both militarily and financially, but state elections in September saw significant gains for parties at both ends of the political spectrum who are critical of expenditure on Ukraine: the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) in Saxony-Anhalt and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and the socialist Left Party in Berlin.
In his speech on Thursday, Merz called out in particular "the AfD and their Russian backers" and promised Ukraine that Germany would not be divided.

articles.title: 'The Night of the UFOs': Remembering the Oct. 4, 1967, skies over Nova Scotia

image.caption: While Shag Harbour is considered Canada's most famous UFO incident, there were many sightings of unexplained objects in the sky over Nova Scotia on Oct. 4, 1967. (CBC)

blocks.text: Nova Scotia·New

While Oct. 4, 1967, is known for the Shag Harbour UFO incident in Nova Scotia, there were many other sightings of unexplained objects in the skies over the province that night, leading it to be known as "The Night of the UFOs."
Besides Shag Harbour, sightings were reported in Dartmouth, Sambro, Wedgeport and elsewhere
Chris Styles was just 12 years old on a clear night when he looked out his bedroom window and spotted a strange light moving along the shoreline a few blocks from his house.
He grabbed his grandfather's binoculars to get a better look and then ran out of the house, much to his dad's dismay, down to the water's edge.
"There's this huge sphere and it was a very dull orange, and it was glowing just like a poker in a fireplace," said Styles about what he saw on Oct. 4, 1967, around 10 p.m. AT.
While that date is best known for a UFO sighting in Shag Harbour in southwestern Nova Scotia, Styles was in Dartmouth, N.S.
Primarily between the Halifax area and southwestern Nova Scotia, people recorded seeing things in the sky that night, which has led ufologists to call it "The Night of the UFOs."

"If you were outside that ... night and you looked up, and for some hours afterwards, you would have seen something," said Styles. "It was a clear night. People were seeing the faintest stars without binoculars."

Styles has written or co-written three books about UFO sightings, including Impact to Contact: The Shag Harbour Incident. He said coverage of Shag Harbour meant other sightings fell out of the press, such as what the crew of the MV Nickerson saw in the waters off Sambro.
Around 9 p.m., Capt. Leo Mersey said he spotted an object with three flashing red lights. The object, which showed up on radar, was about 25 kilometres away.

items: The man who phoned in Canada's most famous UFO sighting became the face of the mystery

blocks.text: "It was very clear that night and we could see the lights of Halifax," Mersey said in a statement he filed with the RCMP.
The radar also showed three objects about 10 kilometres away, but he could not see them.
Around 11 p.m., the object he could see went into the air, but by then had only one red flashing light.
"I had never seen anything like that before but it sounds like the thing they are looking for down off Shelburne or Barrington Passage," Mersey said in the statement, which was taken Oct. 7, 1967.
The RCMP statement, taken by a corporal with the Lunenburg detachment, noted: "Capt. Mersey is considered to be a reliable type individual and bears a good reputation in his community."
But Shag Harbour has long remained the focus, said Styles, in part because of the large witness pool, what authorities said at the time, and the subsequent paper trail left behind.
In Shag Harbour, an object with flashing lights crashed into the waters off the tiny fishing village.
Besides the many eyewitnesses, adding credence to the account was that a responding RCMP officer, Const. Ron O'Brien, described seeing a light from the object floating about 800 metres offshore.
"It was being carried out to sea by the tide and disappeared before we could get a boat to it," he told the Chronicle-Herald in an Oct. 7, 1967, article.

Styles said RCMP officers commandeered two fishing boats to see what was in the water and if there were any survivors, assuming a plane had crashed. They were joined on the boats by local fishermen and other residents.
He said depending on who you talk to, the object either disappeared or submerged, but there was a yellow foam on the water that some say smelled of sulphur.
On Friday, Oct. 6, a naval diving team was brought in, and seven divers searched through the weekend, but reported finding nothing.
The investigation reached the highest levels of National Defence.

An Oct. 6, 1967, memo by Col. W.W. Turner, the director of operations at National Defence headquarters, noted: "The Rescue Co-ordination Centre conducted [a] preliminary investigation and discounted the possibilities that the sighting was produced by an aircraft, flares, floats, or any other known objects."
His son, John Turner, told CBC News his father often mentioned to the family that he received reports of alleged UFO sightings.
"Many were easily discounted as photos of a Frisbee or a hubcap, but he often said others simply could not be explained," Turner wrote by email.

Styles wasn't the only person to see something in Dartmouth on Oct. 4, according to the Chronicle-Herald on Oct. 7, 1967. The newspaper reported that a woman on her way home from work saw a bright, round object in the sky moving from the Halifax-Dartmouth ferry terminal.
"She described it as brighter, more vivid than a star, with an orange hue like a halo around the circumference," the reporter wrote.
The woman looked at it through binoculars when she got home and saw it was not a star.

The newspaper checked with CFB Shearwater's control tower to see if anything was on the radar during the window the woman described. Control tower personnel said no one was monitoring the radar at the time.

articles.title: The King will never live at Buckingham Palace. What does that mean for the monarchy?
articles.summary: While there have been efforts to emphasize that Buckingham Palace will continue to be the working and ceremonial headquarters of the monarchy, the recent confirmation that King Charles won’t be…

image.caption: Members from the Massed Bands of the Guards Division play on the forecourt of Buckingham Palace in London on Sept. 11. (Ben Whitley/Getty Images)

blocks.text: Hello, royal watchers and all those intrigued by what's going on inside the House of Windsor. This is your biweekly dose of royal news and analysis.

For quite a while now, it's been clear that King Charles is quite happy living at Clarence House and has little interest in moving out of that stately home and going down the road to reside in Buckingham Palace.

So it was perhaps not a huge surprise when word emerged that he would never live in that historic central London landmark — even though in ways it has become the most high-profile and visible symbol of the monarchy itself.

While there have been efforts to emphasize that the palace will continue to be the working and ceremonial headquarters of the monarchy, the confirmation that the King won't be living there could also be sending signals about the institution and its future.

"It's a real shift away from what we expect from the monarchy and … it's an example of perhaps slimming down," Craig Prescott, a constitutional expert and lecturer in law at Royal Holloway, University of London, said in an interview.
With fewer senior members of the Royal Family, there is perhaps a move to start to "rationalize some of the properties," he said.

The shift in emphasis for the palace could also be a harbinger of a more subtle but noteworthy shift in focus for the House of Windsor as the monarchy, an institution steeped in tradition, tries to fortify its relevance in a modern world.

"The King will, in effect, use Buckingham Palace … as his office and in a sense go to work every day," said Prescott, who sees it as part of a potential distinction emerging between the institution of the monarchy and the person who holds the role of monarch at any given time, effectively becoming a custodian.

"There seems to be a shift, which perhaps is more modern thinking, because with Elizabeth II, she was the monarchy — the two were totally sort of one in the same, whereas perhaps we're teasing out a distinction between the monarchy and the monarch at any particular time."
Buckingham Palace was built in 1703 and converted into a royal palace in the 1820s.

While it had been the home of every monarch from Queen Victoria up to Elizabeth, no monarch had actually lived there since the COVID-19 pandemic. At that time, Elizabeth moved to Windsor Castle, just as a 10-year, 369-million-pound ($692 million Cdn) refurbishment project at the palace was also underway.

When Charles started his cancer treatment in 2024, there were also some advantages to the royal residence and the royal office being in separate places, Toronto-based royal historian Carolyn Harris said in an interview.

"At a time when there was an enormous amount of concern about King Charles III's health and the aftermath of his cancer diagnosis, the fact that he had a short commute from Clarence House to Buckingham Palace had the effect of keeping him in the public eye without a need for formal public occasions," she said.
"Some of the symbolism that came out of that moment might also have informed this decision."
A shift in royal residences has precedents.

"There have been many periods where an established royal residence that seemed as though it would always be a royal residence — it didn't necessarily suit the needs of the next dynasty or the next generation in the Royal Family," said Harris.

"George III refused to live at Hampton Court, which had been a royal residence all the way from Henry VIII to his grandfather George II, because he didn't have good memories of that palace. He remembered his grandfather … boxing his ears there."

items: King Charles won't live in Buckingham Palace after completion of £369M renovation

blocks.text: Still, the move away from the monarch calling Buckingham Palace home feels significant.

"In the 21st century, this is being treated as a seminal moment as Buckingham Palace is so closely associated with the Royal Family today that we sometimes forget about palaces that no longer exist or mostly no longer exist, such as Whitehall or Greenwich, [which] were at one time the centre of royal power," said Harris.
With the monarch no longer living at Buckingham Palace, it remains to be seen what effect — if any — that will have on public perceptions of the monarchy.

"So many people — when they visit London, [they] visit Buckingham Palace and peer through the gates, watch the changing of the guard … always hoping they might catch a glimpse of a member of the Royal Family," said Harris.

"So it'll be interesting to see if what Buckingham Palace symbolizes transcends whether there are royalty in residence or not, or whether we see … more interest in some of the other royal residences."
Harris isn't writing off Buckingham Palace just yet.
"I think Buckingham Palace's name recognition, its appeal as a tourist destination, I think there's still going to be a lot of interest."
An 'unusual' royal phone call with Canada
As far as royal phone calls go, there don't seem to be many precedents — at least not any calls that get public attention drawn to them.
After Prince William and Prime Minister Mark Carney were on the phone together the other day, their spokespeople let it be known they'd had a chat.

The Prime Minister's Office didn't share any details of what they talked about, but a Kensington Palace spokesperson said the heir to the throne "discussed the enduring strength of the U.K.-Canada relationship" with Carney.
William also expressed his "longstanding affection for Canada and its people," the spokesperson said.
The call "certainly seems to be unusual," royal historian Justin Vovk said via email.
"In most situations like this, the prime minister would be speaking directly with the King as sovereign."
It's also rather unusual that the PMO would release a statement announcing that a phone call had taken place and then provide no details of what was discussed, Vovk said.

"We know that William will not speak about the conversation, so without more information, we have to assume that the PMO disclosed this conversation as an optics exercise and a reminder that Canada maintains close ties with the United Kingdom in no small part because of our shared monarchy."
The call, says Harris, shows that William's diplomatic role is expanding and he's building a "strong rapport" with political figures in the Commonwealth realms along with the United Kingdom.

Harris also noted the public reference to William's feelings toward Canada, a country he first visited as a child with his parents and younger brother, going up the CN Tower in Toronto and visiting Niagara Falls.

"Canada was the first country William and Catherine visited as a married couple and during this visit William quoted his great-grandmother Queen Elizabeth the Queen Mother in 1939, who stated: 'Canada made us.'"
Traditionally, Harris said via email, the heir to the throne has built relationships with Commonwealth prime ministers through royal tours and official engagements.
But there might have been another factor at play in the call between William and Carney.
"There is a personal connection between Prince William and Prime Minister Carney," Harris said.
"Prime Minister Carney's brother, Sean Carney, is chief operating officer at Kensington Palace."
Back to the U.S. and Canada

After spending several days in New York and Washington, D.C., this week, Prince Edward was in Toronto Friday, drawing to a close a North American visit that focused on areas of particular interest to the Duke of Edinburgh.

Youth opportunities and the arts were front and centre in the visit that was scheduled to take him to the Lassonde Art Trail in Toronto, along with engagements supporting the Duke of Edinburgh Awards.

Edward planned to meet with educators, award providers and students at Queen's Park Friday. The Ontario government recently announced it is investing $4 million and expanding access to the award program in schools across the province.
"Talent is everywhere; opportunity is not," Fouzia Younis, British consul general to Toronto, said in a release. "This investment into young people delivers just that: opportunity."

Earlier in the week, Edward was at the Metropolitan Opera in New York meeting representatives of the city's cultural sector. In Baltimore, he visited Western High School, the oldest all-girls public high school in the U.S., as they became a new partner school for the Duke of Edinburgh Award.
While in the Washington area, Edward also visited Mount Vernon in recognition of the 250th anniversary celebrations in the U.S. this year.
Edward's U.S. visit follows the high-profile trip there earlier this year by his elder brother, King Charles.

items: King Charles got a warm welcome from Trump, but how long will the good vibes last?
More 'soft power signals': On heels of King's visit, Prince Edward takes week-long trip to P.E.I., Ontario

blocks.text: Edward is a more frequent royal visitor — he was last in both the U.S. and Canada in 2025.
A brother's swan song for his sister

There is little doubt that Charles Spencer's recent book about his late sister Diana, Princess of Wales — published amid a mad swirl of headlines around its more incendiary claims — adds to the debate and interpretation of her legacy.

Beyond those claims — perhaps the most incendiary being that King Charles said his former wife would soon be forgotten after her death — the book offers new anecdotes and insights into Diana, particularly in the early years she shared with her little brother.

More broadly, Swan Song: Diana, my sister raises more questions over recent history within the upper echelons of the Royal Family, and ultimately reflects the impossibility of ever fully knowing what Diana thought or felt.
